text:
The Jets have now gone seven games without a win (0-5-2), and the second period in Tampa showed how it keeps happening. TBL scored four times in the middle frame, the last two within 56 seconds of each other, and WPG spent the rest of the night chasing a deficit it nearly erased.

Pontus Holmberg was the center of it, with a goal and three assists, including the late empty-looking insurance goal at 18:29 of the third that made it 6-4. He was drafted 156th overall in 2018 and wasn't a point-a-game player in Sweden's top league, yet he, Anthony Cirelli and Brandon Hagel were on the ice for most of the damage and each finished with a goal. The Lightning also created the better chances: 4.34 expected goals (a measure of shot quality) to 2.21, which gave them a 76% deserved-to-win figure, our estimate of how often they win if the shots are replayed. Stuart Skinner allowed 2.0 more goals than his shots called for before Nico Daws relieved him and stopped all nine he faced.

The Jets deserve credit for the third period, when Dylan Samberg, Neal Pionk and Kyle Connor scored to cut a 5-1 hole to 5-4. Pionk's first-period goal came on a 2% chance. But Tampa Bay's power play went 1 for 3 against Winnipeg's 0 for 2, and the comeback came up one goal short. The Jets stay winless in seven. TBL took the points without needing to be perfect, and Andrei Vasilevskiy, who allowed four goals on 2.21 expected, got them anyway.
